stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and no existing spec. Live preview of CMS content across GO, UP, and MX platforms is a complex feature involving real-time rendering and content synchronization. openspec should elaborate requirements and AC first; speckit should then harden with testability, security, and edge-case coverage.

agentContributions.notes: Story requests a new capability — Contentstack Live Preview integration — not a bug fix. The primary attachment point is useContent, the central hook that 236 components call to fetch content. Live Preview SDK must plug into this hook to subscribe to real-time content changes and trigger re-renders in consuming components. Secondary attachment is the app-level Contentstack SDK initialization where the Live Preview client is configured. ACs were empty; VCs derived from description intent.

Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria with a valuable note identifying the two integration points (useContent hook and Contentstack SDK init in context). I authored all 12 ACs from scratch based on that note, the story title/description, and the listed file paths. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1/AC-2 establish the happy-path and graceful-degradation baseline; (2) AC-4 addresses SSR safety and config leakage (security) — critical because ContentstackContext runs at app root; (3) AC-5/AC-6/AC-10 cover error and resilience scenarios (connection drop, malformed data, SDK load failure); (4) AC-7 enforces cross-codebase parity since the story scope is [GO, UP, MX]; (5) AC-8 covers subscription cleanup on unmount; (6) AC-9 prevents stale-data bleed between entries; (7) AC-11 ensures granularity of re-renders; (8) AC-12 specifically covers ContentstackLink since it was called out as an affected file. CAVEAT: I do not have the actual file contents — if useContent uses a caching layer, polling pattern, or if ContentstackContext already has partial Live Preview scaffolding, some ACs may need adjustment. I flagged this in acFlagged.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value. openspec identified the two critical integration points (useContent hook called by 236 components, and ContentstackContext for SDK init) — this is architectural scoping that speckit could not have done on its own. speckit then leveraged that analysis to author 12 verification criteria covering happy path, SSR/security (config leakage), error resilience (connection drop, malformed data, SDK load failure), cross-codebase parity for [GO, UP, MX], subscription cleanup, stale-data prevention, re-render granularity, and ContentstackLink specifically. The contributions are complementary: openspec mapped the surface, speckit hardened it. All five manifest paths exist and are plausible for this change. speckit transparently flagged that it lacked actual file contents, meaning some ACs may need adjustment if caching layers or partial Live Preview scaffolding already exist in useContent or ContentstackContext — this is a legitimate residual risk but the agent self-reported it rather than hiding it. The empty acceptanceCriteria array with acceptanceChanged=false is expected brownfield redaction behavior. No missing manifest paths.
